title: North Dakota AI Laws

reading.body:
North Dakota's only AI law is about political advertising, not about data centers, power, or model development.

HB1167, passed 2025-04-11, requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that use AI to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, and enhancements that do not create a new impersonation, and it defines artificial intelligence for that purpose.

The pattern is narrow and disclosure-based. The state regulates one downstream use of AI, synthetic impersonation in campaign material, and leaves the compute layer untouched. For AI specifically, that means North Dakota has not addressed the parts of the stack this site tracks: the buildings, the power contracts, and the grid interconnections that determine how much model capacity can exist in the state.

What the data does not tell the reader is how the law is enforced, what penalties attach, or whether any other AI-adjacent bill failed or remains pending. It covers one enacted law and nothing about the state's energy or siting posture.

North Dakota has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in North Dakota

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HB1167: Artificial intelligence disclosure statements. passed 2025-04-11

    This North Dakota law requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that contain digital content created in whole or in part with artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts certain uses of artificial intelligence for text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation. It defines artificial intelligence for this purpose.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for North Dakota. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
